memory_candidates.claim: PDF text-extraction glyph loss is selective, not uniform. In the Arisaka-Das-Strassburger 2015 PDF, pdftotext drops the box glyph but renders the and/imp glyphs cleanly. A prior dispatch concluded 'Lemma 4.7(i) and (ii) are literally the same formula' from a corrupted read and landed one Lean lemma for both citations; a direct pdftotext -layout render shows they differ. Rule: when a render looks like it duplicates a numbered statement, re-render before concluding duplication, and cross-check the recovered glyphs against the already-formalized definitions via rfl.

When a formalization defines a context-with-hole and a separate 'pruned' variant of it, verify hole DEPTH agreement at every arity, especially the empty/degenerate case. In Cslib's nested-sequent encoding, InputCtx.fillLhs wraps the hole in an extra .box while outputPruning (= Gamma' ++ Lambda) does not, so the two agree for |Lambda| >= 1 and disagree by one nesting level at |Lambda| = 0 - making the soundness theorem for the rule refutable rather than merely unproved. Symptom to look for: a pre-existing bridging lemma that is restricted to the degenerate case and uses tBox (box A -> A) to strip a level.

Establish the build baseline BEFORE planning work against a 'must stay green' invariant. Task 570's brief asserted lake build was green; a scoped lake build showed the target module fails to compile on a clean tree (non-exhaustive match missing a constructor added in a later phase). A strategic-sorry dispatch can leave a module RED if a sibling constructor was landed without updating its consumer's match.

plan_scope_warning: The task as scoped (build the Lambda-chain induction, then discharge the rule) is necessary but NOT sufficient. The plan MUST also (a) land lemma4_7_ii, (b) repair InputCtx.outputPruning, and (c) discharge NestedProof.cut in nested_sound - otherwise the 'lake build green' invariant is unreachable and the discharged theorem would be unsound.
